paragraphs: Yehudah ben Tabbai: Avot 1:8; Mishnah Chagigah 2:2, 16a. He was exceedingly pious. R. Meir says he was nasi and his colleague Shimon ben Shetach head of the court; the sages say the reverse: there, 16b; Jerusalem Talmud there, chapter 2, halakhah 2, and Jerusalem Sanhedrin 6:6 [Nigmar HaDin, halakhah 9 in Heilprin]. Apparently Shimon ben Shetach was nasi, since he sent Choni the Circle-Drawer, “Were you not Choni, etc.”; see there. He acted like a nasi. Although Chagigah there and the Mishnah in Avot appear to follow R. Meir, that is according to his view, since an anonymous mishnah is his. For the distinction between nasi and head of court, see the end of Moed Katan, Yuchasin in the sequence of generations under Yosi ben Yoezer of Tzeredah, and the general rules in the introduction. He executed a plotting witness to counter the Sadducees' view, but erred. He undertook never to rule except before Shimon ben Shetach, and went every day to weep over the man he had killed until he died: Chagigah 16b; Makkot 5b. Yuchasin, under Yehoshua ben Perachyah and Nittai HaArbeli, writes that Jerusalem Sanhedrin says—the compiler says the passage is found only in Chagigah, chapter 2, halakhah 2—the people of Jerusalem wished to appoint him nasi. He fled to Alexandria. They wrote from great Jerusalem to little Alexandria: “How long will my betrothed sit with you while I sit grieving for him?” He embarked in a ship and told his students, “Do you remember the hostess who received me? What did she lack?” One student said, “My teacher, her eyes were damaged.” He replied, “You have two faults: you suspected me, and you looked at her. Did you think I was asking whether she was beautiful? I meant whether she was fine in her deeds.” End of quotation. Avot DeRabbi Natan, end of chapter 10: he says, “Before I entered high office, if someone told me to ascend, I would pursue him to the utmost. Once I entered, if someone told me to descend, I would pour kettles of hot water over him.” See R. Yehoshua ben Perachyah and R. Yehoshua ben Kefusai, who also said this. Yehudah ben Tabbai and Shimon ben Shetach received from Yehoshua ben Perachyah and Nittai HaArbeli: Avot, chapter 1. They received from them at the beginning of Hasmonean rule, in year 621, 213 of the Temple. Chanamel the Egyptian and Elyoeini ben HaKof lived in his time.
